idiom_name: ast.NodeVisitor and ast.NodeTransformer with PEP 634 class patterns
implementation_notes: The standard library already contains the pattern: ast.parse builds the tree, ast.NodeVisitor drives the walk with visit_<NodeType> hooks, and ast.NodeTransformer rewrites because a visit method may return a replacement node (None deletes it, a list splices it) - the traversal is the base class's and the rule is the override. PEP 634 match makes the shape declarative (case ast.BinOp(left=left, op=ast.Add(), right=ast.Constant(value=0)) binds the pieces directly), so a rule reads like the tree it describes and the classic rule table disappears into match arms. Because the AST is abstract, a rewrite reprints the file and normalises formatting; when comments and layout must survive, the libcst variant is the right tool.
code_sketch:
class DropAddZero(ast.NodeTransformer):
    def visit_BinOp(self, node: ast.BinOp) -> ast.AST:
        node = self.generic_visit(node)            # bottom-up, engine-owned walk
        match node:                                # PEP 634 class patterns
            case ast.BinOp(left=left, op=ast.Add(), right=ast.Constant(value=0)):
                return left                        # x + 0 -> x
        return node

DropAddZero().visit(tree)   # then ast.fix_missing_locations / compile
pitfalls: The stdlib AST drops formatting: rewriting and ast.unparse normalise the whole file, so a transform that must preserve comments or line layout needs the concrete-syntax variant instead.
A NodeTransformer visit method must call generic_visit to descend, and nodes returned without locations break compile() until ast.fix_missing_locations fills lineno and col_offset.

Attribute patterns only match nodes whose fields are present with the expected names and arity, so an unexpected call shape (starargs, keyword-only arguments) silently fails to match and needs a negative fixture.

variants.name: LibCST matchers over concrete syntax (formatting preserved)
variants.idiom_name: libcst.matchers (m.Call, m.Name, ZeroOrMore, MatchMetadata) with MatcherDecoratableTransformer
variants.implementation_notes: LibCST keeps the concrete syntax, so its matchers describe a shape over whitespace-preserving nodes: m.Call(func=m.Name("pred"), args=[m.ZeroOrMore()]) with sequence helpers (ZeroOrMore, AtLeastN, AtMostN), alternation (m.Name("True") | m.Name("False")), inversion, capture (SaveMatchedNode, extract, extractall) and metadata predicates (MatchMetadata on expression context, qualified names or position). matches, findall and replace attempt the pattern; MatcherDecoratableTransformer adds @m.leave and @m.call_if_inside decorators so an action attaches to exactly the matching subtrees, and the round-trip keeps spacing, comments and parentheses. Use this variant when the rewrite must be style-preserving; keep the stdlib variant when no dependency is acceptable.
pitfalls: Matchers default every attribute to DoNotCare, so a matcher smaller than intended matches far more nodes; state the shape explicitly or add a metadata predicate before attaching a rewrite.
The CST is a tree over tokens: a rebuilt node must carry the original whitespace fields (whitespace_before, parens, semicolon) or the output loses spacing and the transform stops being idempotent.
Metadata-dependent matchers need a MetadataWrapper, otherwise matches raises LookupError because the metadata resolver was never provided.
